Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Can a short trace be assumed electrically safe?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Discontinuity, return path, coupling, and load conditions also matter.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A package trace and its return path form an electrical loop; geometry influences impedance and noise. Trace the visual in order: signal trace; reference plane; return current. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: On a proposed RDL route, mark the nearest reference path. A layer transition that breaks continuity deserves an explicit check.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: On a proposed RDL route, mark the nearest reference path. A layer transition that breaks continuity deserves an explicit check. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: Does routing relief guarantee a better design?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Power integrity and local heating may worsen; assess both under the same load.
Visual: The diagram lists the conditions to inspect without marking the answer.
[Sources]

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A lower peak temperature may coexist with greater warpage or a routing-rule violation; hard constraints and objectives must be separated. Trace the visual in order: thermal target; warpage limit; routing rule. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic A is 2 K cooler but fails an assumed routing rule; B meets the rule with a higher yet acceptable temperature. Reject A under that hard rule. Boundary: The 2 K comparison is synthetic teaching data.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing
